Example catalogue

This catalogue covers 89 tracked programs, including 50 mathematics programs. Each entry gives the reviewed source behavior, the authored test registrations and the outcome measured when the program was run at the release SHA.

Measurement snapshot for these 89 programs at release SHA 60f345def (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release build, macOS arm64, measured 2026-10-09) in native JIT and native AOT. 48 completed in both modes; 31 of those printed their own verdict RESULT: ALL PASS with Failed: 0 in both modes, and the other 17 print diagnostics or a receipt without a RESULT: line (status RAN-OK: exit 0, no runtime-error line; the entry quotes the output). Without a passing verdict at this SHA: H₂ frequency from quantum-backend geometry differences, Quantum natural-gradient comparison, H₂ variational quantum optimization (its entry shows the output). Not run: Exact algebraic automatic differentiation, Packed exact algebraic multiplication, Exact algebraic computation across matrices, constraints and live rows, Coupled exact implicit differentiation, Maintained exact incremental objective and gradient, Exact algebraic matrix calculus, Exact algebraic solve pullback and HVP, Certified exact convex quadratic programs and active-set pullbacks, Exact algebraic reverse-mode pullback and HVP, Exact live ridge fit and regularization sensitivity, Exact sparse algebraic curvature, Exact simple eigenvalue branch and projector, Guarded exact low-rank updates, Exact restart equivalence for a standing DBSP circuit, Exact a-posteriori linear solve admission, Cup products and Bockstein on finite-group nerves, Nonabelian order-eight cohomology rings, Maintained named-axis tensor contractions, Exact derivatives and finite changes of a bounded polynomial, Descent double complexes and hypercohomology, Finite categories and Kan extensions, Integral plus construction on a finite site, Sheaf cohomology of finite spaces, Cup-square obstruction in four-manifold models, The functor of points: one program over many rings, Integral homology and twists of order-eight groups, Parametric finite-group homology receipts, Grothendieck constructions and homotopy colimits, Horn fillers and low homotopy groups, Cyclotomic Reidemeister torsion of lens complexes, Internal logic of finite presheaf categories, Sheafification, reflector and Kan descent, Exact cyclotomic Turaev–Viro state sums, Crossed-module nerves and Postnikov data, Generate a standalone specialized program, Nested exact differentiation over a certified combined field, Bell circuit OpenQASM 3 export, Maintained grouped AD loss and gradients (the entry states why). Wall times measured with 6 programs running concurrently on a shared machine; CPU user/sys from wait4.

The mathematics guide gives each mathematical program’s published result, references, algorithm, domain, arithmetic, checks, limits and measured values. The Navier–Stokes guide and AI mathematics guide retain their explanatory narratives and references.

The general examples runner discovers 86 flat programs and compiles/runs them with native AOT. 4 require ESHKOL_QUANTUM_ENABLED=ON; 0 current paths match the existing proprietary/unreleased exclusion patterns. The 3 nested artifact generator is outside that glob. A successful process is distinct from an asserted mathematical verdict: PASS below means the program printed its own RESULT: ALL PASS with Failed: 0; RAN-OK means a program without a self-verdict exited 0 with no runtime-error line.

The NS/IPM CMake lists declare native JIT/AOT tests under ESHKOL_BUILD_TESTS AND TARGET eshkol-run. The bytecode VM runs four of the cohomology programs under its own CTest entries; VM support for the other examples is not claimed here.

For manual AOT commands below, create .scratch/example-manual once from the repository root.

To check documentation drift: python3 scripts/build_example_catalogue.py --check. After deliberate source/semantic review, update the catalogue, re-run the examples, ingest the receipts with --ingest, and run --write; the generator never updates fingerprints or executes examples, and a measurement whose source SHA-256 no longer matches fails the check.

Language and application examples

These descriptions report implemented checks or printed diagnostics; output prose is not treated as an assertion.

Exact algebraic automatic differentiation

Source: algebraic_ad.esk. SHA-256: 75623281baa24793f65abd9fc9d0d3092916cc40299e699af5e48b158f1366df.

Purpose: Differentiate a local algebraic branch exactly over Q(cuberoot(2)).

Implemented algorithm: Lift the simple root of y^3=2+t through a fourth-order Taylor carrier using bounded nilpotent Newton steps; retain hyperdual derivatives of a zero-primal field relation.

Domain and parameters: One selected cubic real field; Taylor order four and a four-coefficient hyperdual carrier.

Arithmetic: Exact rational power-basis field coefficients and nilpotent AD operations; no floating approximation or finite differences.

Checks in the source: Six assertions check the entire cubic equation, independently derived first/second/fourth derivatives, nonzero derivatives of a zero-primal relation and zero finite-difference evaluations; explicit RESULT: PASS or nonzero exit.

Limits: The supplied simple root is already in the selected field; no scalar root search, new field extension, general transcendental AD or arbitrary-function compiler transformation. Existing exact scalar arithmetic limits apply.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib plus source-tree core.ad.algebraic and core.algebraic_field.

Measured at 60f345def (Eshkol Compiler v1.3.6-evolve, Release, macOS arm64): NOT-RUN. New example pending configured release qualification; local focused evidence is separate.

Implementation/check anchors: line 1, line 8, line 14, line 23, line 29.

./build/eshkol-run -r examples/algebraic_ad.esk
./build/eshkol-run -L./build examples/algebraic_ad.esk -o .scratch/example-manual/algebraic_ad && .scratch/example-manual/algebraic_ad

Packed exact algebraic multiplication

Purpose: Multiply exact values in Q(cuberoot(2)) using a preflighted packed plan.

Implemented algorithm: Compile the field multiplication into a sparse integer table, preflight signed-32-bit bounds, then reconstruct exact rational coefficients.

Domain and parameters: One selected cubic real field; a single exact generator product.

Arithmetic: Exact rational power-basis coefficients and native integer multiply-accumulate; no floating conversion.

Checks in the source: Compares packed alpha squared with scalar exact algebraic multiplication; prints RESULT: PASS.

Limits: Only admitted domains within component, term, batch and signed-32-bit bounds; no performance claim from operation counters.

Exact algebraic computation across matrices, constraints and live rows

Source: algebraic_frontiers.esk. SHA-256: 1d7ee24f1d77b48899c75708938a3d138229ebce0508025815ab10de23392497.

Purpose: Connect certified field composition, matrix calculus, coupled implicit roots, packed multiplication, sparse curvature and live exact parameter gradients.

Implemented algorithm: Use the shared coefficient-domain adapter and retained exact residuals; polynomial sufficient statistics absorb signed row edits while explicit Taylor carriers differentiate live parameters.

Domain and parameters: Selected degree-six Q(sqrt(2),cuberoot(2)); two-variable coupled constraints, second-order jets and a two-parameter squared affine loss.

Arithmetic: Exact rational power-basis and nilpotent coefficients; preflighted native integer products; no floating approximation or finite differences.

Checks in the source: Eight assertions compare exact matrix/root/product/curvature/loss/gradient formulas and zero row replay/finite-difference counts; explicit RESULT: PASS or nonzero exit.

Limits: Bounded reference constructions; supplied simple roots, complete declared sparsity and polynomial-only maintained plans. Packed products require certified signed-32-bit admission. No global nonlinear solver, arbitrary loss transformation or flat-RSS claim.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and source-tree exact algebraic modules.

Coupled exact implicit differentiation

Source: algebraic_implicit.esk. SHA-256: 8d8fcf23e41044e50869126efed1d3289aeed4796849c1647030ef8274beb169.

Purpose: Lift a supplied simple branch of a coupled polynomial system through an exact Taylor carrier.

Implemented algorithm: Derive the polynomial Jacobian, factor its primal matrix once, and reuse it for exact nilpotent corrections.

Domain and parameters: Two coupled equations over Q(sqrt(2)); order-four Taylor carrier at the supplied branch (sqrt(2), sqrt(2)).

Arithmetic: Exact rational power-basis coefficients and exact Taylor derivatives; no finite differences.

Checks in the source: Three assertions check coupled components, the full vector residual and exact Taylor derivatives from the binomial expansion; explicit RESULT: PASS or nonzero exit.

Limits: Demonstrates local lifting around one supplied simple branch; it does not search roots or prove global uniqueness.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib plus source-tree core.ad.algebraic and core.ad.algebraic_implicit.

Maintained exact incremental objective and gradient

Source: algebraic_incremental.esk. SHA-256: 2e7f154bbcfb5073f973d61ec7cef7a0e115524983ad20ae550a70238a3ade4c.

Purpose: Maintain an exact least-squares objective and parameter gradient across a signed row replacement and parameter update.

Implemented algorithm: Compile a bounded polynomial in row and parameter variables, update its row moments from a DBSP Z-set delta, then evaluate its live exact gradient at the new parameters.

Domain and parameters: A two-parameter affine residual over the certified real field Q(sqrt(2)); two initial rows and one signed replacement.

Arithmetic: Exact rational power-basis coefficients and exact algebraic AD; no floating conversion or finite differences.

Checks in the source: Compares the maintained objective and both gradient coordinates with an independently written full exact scan of the updated rows; checks that parameter updates replay no rows.

Limits: The expression language is bounded to exact polynomial syntax with degree at most eight. The example demonstrates semantics and work counters, not speed or memory limits.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib plus source-tree core.dbsp, core.algebraic_domain and core.ad.algebraic_incremental.

Exact algebraic matrix calculus

Source: algebraic_matrix_calculus.esk. SHA-256: fa1ffb035789f75090b14da972533dd7d228a6032b5330d87a93d1d127c41bfe.

Purpose: Solve exact matrix systems over a selected real number field and its Taylor carrier.

Implemented algorithm: Factor the field matrix once, reuse the exact LU for independent right-hand sides, then solve Taylor coefficients recursively through the same bottom-field factorization.

Domain and parameters: A 2x2 system over Q(sqrt(2)) and the corresponding order-four Taylor carrier at x=2.

Arithmetic: Exact rational power-basis coefficients and exact Taylor coefficients; no floating approximation or finite differences.

Checks in the source: Three assertions check both exact inverse columns, reused bottom-field factorization, and the first three derivatives of the Taylor solution; explicit RESULT: PASS or nonzero exit.

Limits: The example demonstrates a small dense system and one Taylor carrier. It does not claim sparse, rectangular solve, larger workload or compiler AD coverage.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib plus source-tree core.algebraic_field, core.ad.algebraic and core.algebraic_linalg.

Exact algebraic solve pullback and HVP

Source: algebraic_pullback.esk. SHA-256: 680b018db65455ce5b56b56ea05a786f5f39153f3040ea2607a35b9eb118084b.

Purpose: Differentiate an equation-defined exact solve over Q(sqrt(2)) and check its value, gradient and Hessian-vector product.

Implemented algorithm: Solve x*theta=1 on the exact reverse tape, then compare its pullback and forward-over-reverse HVP with independent closed-form field values.

Domain and parameters: One parameter theta=sqrt(2) over its certified real quadratic field.

Arithmetic: Exact rational power-basis coefficients and algebraic operations; no floating conversion or finite differences.

Checks in the source: Three in-program assertions check the exact solution, derivative -1/theta^2 and HVP 2/theta^3. The program prints RESULT: PASS only after all assertions pass.

Limits: This is a one-dimensional exact linear solve over one supplied field; it makes no claim about general compiler transformations or speed.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib plus source-tree core.ad.algebraic_pullback.

Certified exact convex quadratic programs and active-set pullbacks

Source: algebraic_qp.esk. SHA-256: 6759d5a2cd9c37b46a0258755ea31ad7d60b77f7f4b3bc7226b04a57954b97ad.

Purpose: Solve small strictly convex quadratic programs over an exact algebraic field, check KKT certificates, and differentiate stable active branches.

Implemented algorithm: Enumerate inequality active sets, solve the exact KKT system, verify stationarity and complementary slackness, and reuse the transposed factor for parameter pullbacks.

Domain and parameters: A two-variable equality-constrained problem over Q(sqrt(2)) and a one-variable rational bound-constrained problem.

Arithmetic: Exact rational and algebraic field operations; no floating conversion or finite differences.
